## Financial‑Operations Strategy **Goal:** Keep the existing EU ↔ Gulf ↔ Southeast‑Asia ↔ Latin‑America remittance corridors profitable **while** building a scalable framework for new lanes that can survive — different licences, KYC/AML regimes, settlement‑currency rules, capital‑control regimes, uneven partner‑tech maturity, and widely‑varying margins. > **Key Guiding Principle** – **“Regulatory‑First, Risk‑Adjusted, Partner‑Optimised”** > 1. **Regulatory‑First** – obtain the minimum‑necessary licences and a uniform compliance backbone that can be “plug‑and‑play’’ for each jurisdiction. > 2. **Risk‑Adjusted** – model settlement‑risk, liquidity‑risk and capital‑control exposure per corridor and price margins accordingly. > 3. **Partner‑Optimised** – choose banking/settlement partners on a **technical‑maturity / economics** matrix and drive a **partner‑enablement programme** that lifts lower‑maturity partners toward a common API standard. --- ## 1. Regulatory & Licensing Landscape (2026) | Bloc | Core Regulatory Body(s) | Typical Licence(s) Required | KYC/AML Key Rules | Settlement‑Currency Constraints | Capital‑Control Highlights | |------|------------------------|----------------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------| | **EU** (including UK‑EIR) | ESMA, local Central Banks, FCA (UK) | E‑money Institution (EMI), Payment Institution (PI) – **PSD2** | 5‑day customer‑due‑diligence, “Travel Rule” (FATF), GDPR‑linked data‑privacy | Euro‑zone: SEPA‑Euro only for Euro‑zone clients; cross‑border can use any **authorized currency** with AML‑screening | No formal FX caps, but **ECB‑SRM** requires daily liquidity reporting for cross‑border settlement | | **Gulf (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait)** | Central Bank of UAE, SAMA, Qatar Central Bank | **Money‑Transfer Licence** (MTL) or **E‑money licence**; often a **local sponsor** required | “Know‑Your‑Customer” must be **Arabic‑language**; high‑risk‑political‑exposure checks; **Shar‑i’ah compliance** for suspicious‑activity reporting | Settlement usually in **local currency (AED, SAR, QAR, etc.)**; limited to **domestic‑currency pairs** (USD‑AED, USD‑SAR) – **FX‑conversion** must be performed by a licensed bank | **Capital‑control** on outbound USD flows > US$50 k per transaction (subject to “Sanction‑Free” flag) | | **Southeast Asia** (Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Philippines) | MAS (SG), BNM (MY), OJK (ID), etc. | **Standard Chartered Licence** (SCL) for e‑money / payments; **Electronic Money Institution (EMI)** in SG | “Risk‑Based Approach” – tiered KYC (Level 1/2/3) + **PEP screening**; **Data‑localisation** (Indonesia mandates local storage) | **Multiple settlement currencies** allowed (SGD, IDR, VND, PHP, USD) but each regulator caps **single‑currency settlement** to 90 % of transaction volume; must disclose FX‑rate source | **Capital‑control** in Indonesia (max USD 250 k per day outbound) and Vietnam (monthly cap USD 100 k) – need local‑bank pre‑approval | | **Latin America** (Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Argentina) | Central Bank of Brazil (BCB), Banco de México, etc. | **Payment Institution** (Brazil – “Instituição de Pagamento”) or **FinTech licence**; often a **local partner** required for cross‑border | **“Know‑Your‑Customer”** requires **CPF/CNPJ** for Brazil, **CURP** for Mexico; **Anti‑Money‑Laundering** (AML) thresholds lower (US$10 k) in Brazil; **GDPR‑like** data‑privacy in Argentina (Law 27.275) | Settlement typically in **local currency** (BRL, MXN, COP, PEN) – **FX** must be done by a **licensed exchange**; **dual‑currency (local/USD)** allowed only with a “currency‑exchange licence” | **Capital‑control**: Brazil’s **IOF tax** (0.38 % on outbound FX) and **monthly outbound limit** US$50 k per individual; Mexico has **FX‑reporting** but no hard caps | > **Take‑away:** The firm must hold **four core licences** (EU PI/EMI, Gulf MTL, SEA EMI, LATAM Payment Institution) and **use local “sponsor” or “partner” banks** to meet jurisdiction‑specific settlement‑currency and capital‑control rules. --- ## 2. Unified Compliance Architecture (RegTech‑First) | Layer | Function | Technology & Process | Regional Adaptation | |-------|----------|----------------------|----------------------| | **Identity‑Onboarding Hub** | Centralised KYC/AML engine, supports **multi‑jurisdictional data‑models** | • **Identity‑Verification API** (e.g., Onfido, Trulioo) with **local data‑source adapters** (e‑ID, national ID).
• **Rule‑Engine** (Camunda / Drools) hosts **jurisdiction‑specific AML scenarios** (PEP, sanctions, transaction‑size). | - EU: GDPR‑compliant storage, 2‑year retention.
- Gulf: Arabic‑language data fields, “Sharia‑compliant” risk flags.
- SEA: Tier‑ed KYC (Level 1‑3) per MAS/BNM rules.
- LATAM: CPF/CNPJ validator, local tax‑ID enrichment. | | **Transaction‑Screening Service** | Real‑time sanctions / watch‑list checks (FATF, OFAC, EU‑Sanctions) | • **Graph‑based watch‑list DB** (Neo4j) for rapid look‑ups.
• **AI‑risk‑scorer** (Explainable‑ML) for “low‑risk” auto‑approve vs. “high‑risk” manual review. | Configurable thresholds per bloc (e.g., EU = 0.7, Gulf = 0.8). | | **Compliance‑Workflow Engine** | Case management for manual reviews, audit trail, regulator‑ready reports | • **Secure ticketing** (ServiceNow/Custom) with **role‑based access** (Compliance Officer, AML Analyst).
• **Automated SAR filing** to local regulator via API where available. | Auto‑escalation to local sponsor bank’s AML team where required (Gulf, LATAM). | | **Data‑Governance Layer** | Data residency, encryption, consent tracking | • **Hybrid cloud** – EU‑region (Azure EU), Gulf‑region (Azure Gulf), SEA (AWS Singapore), LATAM (Google Cloud Brazil).
• **Field‑level encryption**; **Consent‑Log** stored per GDPR, LGPD, PDPA. | Guarantees “data‑localisation” mandates (Indonesia, Brazil). | | **Reporting & Auditing Dashboard** | KPI, compliance metrics, audit logs, regulator‑ready extracts | • **Power‑BI / Looker** dashboards with per‑bloc filters.
• **Export‑as‑XML** for regulator portals. | One‑click generation of **EU‑TSR**, **GCC‑AML**, **MAS‑Monthly**, **BCB‑FX** reports. | > **Result:** A **single compliance platform** (core) with **plug‑in adapters** for each jurisdiction, dramatically reducing duplicated effort and licence‑maintenance cost. --- ## 3. Settlement‑Risk & Liquidity Management ### 3.1 Core Principles | Principle | Implementation | |-----------|----------------| | **Local‑Currency Settlement** wherever legally required | Maintain **regional liquidity pools** in EUR, AED, SAR, SGD, IDR, BRL, MXN, etc. | | **FX‑Hedging at Margin‑Optimal Frequency** | Use **FX‑forward contracts** and **non‑deliverable forwards (NDFs)** aligned with daily settlement windows; hedge **only the net exposure** after intra‑bloc netting. | | **Dual‑Bank Settlement Model** | **Primary settlement bank** (high‑tech, low‑cost) + **fallback “bridge bank”** (local partner) to mitigate operational outages. | | **Capital‑Control Buffer** | Pre‑allocate **regulatory‑approved capital** (e.g., 5 % of daily outbound volume) in a **restricted‑purpose account** that can be instantly moved under local approval. | | **Real‑Time Settlement Engine** | Deploy a **micro‑service** (e.g., **ISO‑20022** API) that executes **instant FX** and **settlement** in < 5 seconds for high‑volume corridors (EU ↔ Gulf). | ### 3.2 Corridor‑Specific Settlement Blueprint | Corridor | Settlement Currency(s) | Liquidity‑Pool Size (10 M USD‑equiv) | Hedging Tool | Capital‑Control Treatment | |----------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------|---------------------------| | **EU → Gulf** | EUR → AED/SAR (via USD bridge) | €5 M (EU) / AED 4 M (Gulf) | NDF on USD‑AED, USD‑SAR; **Daily forward** to lock rate | Outbound USD > $50 k flagged → **pre‑authorisation** via Gulf sponsor bank | | **Gulf → EU** | AED/SAR → EUR (USD bridge) | AED 4 M / €5 M | **FX‑forward** on USD‑EUR, **FX‑option** for vol‑spike | Inbound USD caps lifted if **local bank** certifies compliance | | **EU → SEA** | EUR → SGD/IDR/VND/PH‑(USD) | €3 M (EU) / SGD 6 M (SG) | **NDF** for IDR, VND; **FX‑swap** for SGD | Indonesia daily outbound USD ≤ $250 k → **pre‑allocated local pool** | | **SEA → EU** | Local‑currency → EUR (via USD) | USD 5 M (regional) / €7 M (EU) | **FX‑forward** on USD‑EUR; **FX‑option** for high‑vol markets | Vietnam monthly USD ≤ $100 k → **monthly limit manager** | | **LATAM → EU** | BRL/MXN/PEN → EUR (USD bridge) | BRL 4 M / MXN 5 M / €6 M | **NDF** for BRL‑USD, MXN‑USD; **FX‑forward** for EUR | Brazil IOF tax auto‑applied; MXN caps managed via **Bank‑approved quota** | | **EU → LATAM** | EUR → BRL/MXN/PEN (USD bridge) | €6 M / BRL 5 M | Same tools as above | Same capital‑control handling (tax, quotas) | > **Liquidity‑Pool Funding:** Use **core‑bank credit lines** (Euro‑area syndicated facility) and **regional bank credit lines** (Gulf‑region, SEA, LATAM) to fund pools. Set **interest‑rate spread** based on corridor margin (see Section 4). --- ## 4. Partner‑Economics & Technical Enablement ### 4.1 Partner‑Selection Matrix | Partner Tier | Technical Maturity | Economic Terms | Typical Role | Example Partners (2026) | |--------------|-------------------|----------------|--------------|-------------------------| | **Tier 1 – “Smart‑Bank”** | Full ISO‑20022, real‑time API, sandbox access, 99.9 % uptime | **Revenue‑share 20 %** of net margin, **cost‑plus** settlement fee (0.05 % of value) | Primary settlement, FX execution, compliance‑screening | BNP Paribas (EU), Emirates NBD (Gulf), DBS (SEA), Banco do Brasil (LATAM) | | **Tier 2 – “Legacy‑Bank”** | Batch file (MT‑103/MT‑202), 1‑day latency, limited API | **Revenue‑share 15 %**, higher settlement fee (0.10 %) | Backup settlement, large‑ticket processing | UniCredit (EU), National Commercial Bank (UAE), BNI (Indonesia), Bancomer (Mexico) | | **Tier 3 – “FinTech‑Overlay”** | API‑first, programmable money, token‑isation, crypto‑friendly | **Revenue‑share 12‑18 %**, **per‑transaction fee** (flat $0.30) | Front‑end payment collection, on‑ramp/off‑ramp, digital‑wallet integration | TransferWise (now Wise), Rapyd, Binance‑Pay, PayU (LATAM) | | **Tier 4 – “Bridge/Correspondent”** | Limited connectivity, manual SWIFT, no API | **Revenue‑share 10 %**, **high fee** (0.25 %) | “Last‑mile” for low‑volume corridors, compliance‑audit support | Small regional banks, credit‑unions | > **Economic Target:** Keep **overall corridor net margin** > 2 % after partner fees, FX cost, and compliance overhead. ### 4.2 Partner‑Enablement Programme 1. **API‑Standardisation Kit** – ISO‑20022‑based **JSON** payloads, **OAuth 2.0** security, **OpenAPI** spec shared with all partners. 2. **Technical Maturity Scorecard** – quarterly assessment; tier‑up partners who meet **≥ 90 %** of the spec (automatic fee reduction). 3. **Co‑Funding of Sandbox** – allocate **$250 k** per region to help Tier‑2/3 banks build real‑time APIs; ROI measured by **settlement‑time reduction** (target < 5 sec). 4. **Revenue‑Sharing Review** – annual renegotiation based on **volume‑weighting**; high‑volume corridors (EU ↔ Gulf) move toward **cost‑plus** model, low‑volume corridors stay **revenue‑share**. --- ## 5. Margin & Pricing Model (Cost‑Based + Risk‑Adjusted) | Cost Component | How it is Calculated | Weight in Pricing (example) | |----------------|---------------------|----------------------------| | **Licensing & Reg‑Compliance** | Fixed annual licence fee + per‑transaction compliance cost (average $0.02) | 15 % | | **Partner Settlement Fee** | Tier‑specific fee (see Table 4.1) + FX‑spread | 30 % | | **FX‑Hedging Cost** | Forward points + option premium / transaction value | 20 % | | **Capital‑Control Buffer Cost** | Opportunity cost of locked‑up capital (average 2 % p.a.) | 10 % | | **Operational Overhead** | Cloud, monitoring, staff, fraud‑prevention | 15 % | | **Profit Margin** | Target **≥ 2 %** net after all above | 10 % | > **Dynamic Pricing Engine** – a **micro‑service** that pulls real‑time cost inputs (FX forward curve, partner fee APIs, compliance‑cost per‑transaction) and outputs the **customer‑visible price** (exchange rate + fee). The engine enforces **minimum‑margin thresholds** per corridor (e.g., EU ↔ Gulf min 2.5 %, LATAM ↔ EU min 1.8 %) to protect profitability. --- ## 6. Risk Management Framework | Risk Category | Primary Exposure | Mitigation Controls | |---------------|------------------|---------------------| | **Regulatory Risk** | License revocation, sanction breaches | • **Regulatory Calendar** (auto‑reminders for filing, capital‑adequacy reports).
• **RegTech** alerts for rule‑change (e.g., EU‑PSD3 draft). | | **Settlement‑Risk** | Counter‑party default, FX settlement fail | • **Dual‑Bank** model, **real‑time netting** engine.
• **Credit limit monitoring** per partner (auto‑pause on breach). | | **Capital‑Control Risk** | Outbound caps, sudden policy shifts | • **Capital‑Control Buffer** (pre‑authorised cash).
• **Dynamic routing** (switch to alternative corridor). | | **Operational / Tech Risk** | API downtime, data‑loss, cyber‑attack | • **Zero‑trust network**, **SOC‑2** compliance, **API‑gateway throttling**.
• **Disaster‑Recovery (DR) site** per region (fail‑over < 30 sec). | | **Fraud / Money‑Laundering** | Synthetic IDs, circular transactions | • **AI‑risk‑scorer**, **behavioural analytics**, **real‑time transaction monitoring**.
• **Manual escalation** to local sponsor bank AML team. | | **Liquidity Risk** | Insufficient local‑currency pool | • **Liquidity Management Dashboard** (real‑time pool balances).
• **Automated borrowing** from central credit line when pool < 20 % of daily forecast. | > **Key Metric – “Risk‑Adjusted Net Margin (RANM)”** = (Net Margin – Expected Loss from each risk category). RANM must stay **> 1 %** for a corridor to stay open. --- ## 7. Expansion Roadmap (2026‑2028) | Year | Milestone | Action | Expected Impact | |------|-----------|--------|-----------------| | **2026 Q1** | **Core Platform Launch** (RegTech hub, settlement engine) | Deploy in EU & Gulf (first two corridors) | Baseline compliance cost ↓ 30 % | | **2026 Q2** | **Partner‑Upgrade Sprint** (Tier‑2 banking API enablement) | Co‑fund sandbox with 3 Gulf banks & 2 SEA banks | Settlement latency ↓ 70 % | | **2026 Q3** | **Capital‑Control Buffer** activation for Indonesia & Brazil | Pre‑authorize $10 M pooled funds per region | Outbound cap breaches ↓ 90 % | | **2026 Q4** | **New Corridor Pilot** – **EU ↔ Mexico** | Obtain Mexican “FinTech” licence, integrate Banca Azteca as Tier‑3 partner | Test regulatory‑flex model, add $12 M ARR | | **2027 H1** | **Dynamic Pricing Engine** goes live across all corridors | Real‑time cost‑feed integration | Margin volatility ↓ 15 % | | **2027 H2** | **Regulatory‑Change Automation** – AI‑driven rule extraction from new EU‑PSD3 drafts | Reduce manual rule‑coding time from weeks to days | Compliance lag < 48 h | | **2028 Q1** | **Full‑Corridor Coverage** – Add **EU ↔ Vietnam**, **Gulf ↔ Peru** | Leverage existing platform; rely on Tier‑2 banks after API upgrade | Total cross‑border volume + 45 % | | **2028 H2** | **Strategic Review** – Consolidate **Tier‑1** partners, drop under‑performing Tier‑4 banks | Re‑negotiate revenue‑share, re‑allocate liquidity | Cost‑to‑serve ↓ 12 % | --- ## 8. Governance & Operating Model | Committee | Frequency | Scope | Decision Rights | |----------|-----------|-------|-----------------| | **Global AI‑Col‑Council** (CEO, CFO, Chief Regulatory Officer, Head of Payments Ops) | Monthly | Overall strategy, capital allocation, major licensing decisions | Approve new licences, major partner contracts | | **Regional Regulation Boards** (EU, Gulf, SEA, LATAM) | Bi‑monthly | Local licence renewals, KYC policy tweaks, capital‑control liaison | Sign off any region‑specific compliance changes | | **Partner‑Performance Review Board** | Quarterly | Tier‑up/down decisions, fee renegotiation, technical maturity | Adjust partner tier, set fee schedule | | **Risk‑Ops Committee** | Weekly | Real‑time risk flags, liquidity shortfalls, fraud incidents | Issue stop‑payment orders, adjust limits | | **Product & Pricing Council** | Monthly | Pricing engine parameters, margin thresholds, new‑corridor proposals | Approve price changes across corridors | > **Reporting:** A **central “Operations Dashboard”** (Power‑BI) feeds live KPI to all committees: **Volume, Net Margin, RANM, Compliance‑Cost, Partner‑Uptime, Capital‑Control Utilisation**. --- ## 9. Technology Stack (2026‑Ready) | Layer | Vendor / Tool | Reason | |------|---------------|--------| | **Cloud Infra** | Azure EU, Azure Gulf, AWS Singapore, Google Cloud Brazil | Data‑residency, compliance, high‑availability | | **API‑Gateway** | Kong + OIDC | Centralised security, rate‑limiting, observability | | **Compliance Engine** | **Trulioo** (global ID verif.) + **Finastra AML Suite** (customizable rule engine) | Multi‑jurisdiction KYC, AI‑risk‑scoring | | **Settlement Core** | **Corda‑based DLT** for immutable settlement logs (inter‑bank) + **ISO‑20022 micro‑service** | Guarantees auditability, easy integration with legacy banks | | **FX Hedging** | **Bloomberg Trade Order Management System (TOMS)** + **FX‑Options Platform (Murex)** | Real‑time pricing, automated hedge execution | | **Data‑Lake / Analytics** | **Snowflake** (multi‑cloud) + **Looker** | Centralised reporting, compliance analytics | | **Security** | **Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR** for SOAR, **HashiCorp Vault** for secret management | Zero‑trust, rapid incident response | | **Monitoring** | **Prometheus + Grafana** for services; **Splunk** for logs | SLA tracking, proactive alerts | > **Future‑Proofing:** All core services expose **REST + gRPC** and **OpenAPI** specs, enabling easy plug‑in of new fintech partners or **stable‑coin gateways** (e.g., USDC on regulated DLT) when regulatory clearance arrives. --- ## 10. KPIs & Success Dashboard | KPI | Target (12 mo) | Measurement Frequency | |-----|----------------|-----------------------| | **Cross‑border Volume** | + 30 % YoY (total USD‑equiv) | Monthly | | **Net Margin per Corridor** | EU‑Gulf ≥ 2.5 %
EU‑SEA ≥ 2.0 %
EU‑LATAM ≥ 1.8 % | Quarterly | | **Compliance‑Cost % of Revenue** | ≤ 10 % | Quarterly | | **Partner‑Uptime (ISO‑20022 API)** | ≥ 99.5 % | Real‑time | | **Capital‑Control Utilisation** | ≤ 70 % of allocated buffer | Weekly | | **RANM (Risk‑Adjusted Net Margin)** | ≥ 1 % for every corridor | Quarterly | | **Customer‑Satisfaction (NPS)** | > 55 | Bi‑annual | | **Regulatory Audit Findings** | Zero material | Annual | --- ## 11. Executive Summary & Recommendations 1. **Secure the Four Core Licences** (EU PI/EMI, Gulf MTL, SEA EMI, LATAM Payment Institution) *once* and embed them in a **global AI‑Collaboration Charter** that mandates “human‑in‑the‑loop” for all client‑impact decisions. 2. **Deploy a unified RegTech platform** with modular adapters for each jurisdiction—it cuts compliance staff by **≈35 %** and eliminates duplicated KYC workflows. 3. **Create regional liquidity pools** in the required settlement currencies, backed by a **dual‑bank model** and a **pre‑authorised capital‑control buffer** to survive sudden FX caps. 4. **Adopt a tiered partner‑economics model** (Tier 1‑4). Prioritise **Tier 1 “Smart‑Banks”** for high‑margin, high‑volume corridors; use **Tier 2/3 partners** to expand low‑volume lanes while still meeting SLA targets. 5. **Institutionalise a dynamic pricing engine** that pulls real‑time costs (FX, partner fees, compliance) and enforces a **minimum‑margin guardrail** per corridor. 6. **Implement a risk‑adjusted net‑margin (RANM) metric** to continuously evaluate whether a corridor should stay open, be re‑priced, or be re‑engineered. 7. **Launch the platform in two “anchor” corridors** (EU ↔ Gulf, EU ↔ SEA) in 2026 Q1–Q4, then roll out additional corridors (Latin‑America, Vietnam, Mexico) with the same compliance core but local partner upgrades. 8. **Governance:** Set up a **global‑regional dual committee structure** for licensing, compliance, partner performance, and risk monitoring; feed a **central dashboard** to all decision‑makers. 9. **Technology:** Leverage **cloud‑native ISO‑20022 micro‑services**, a **Corda‑based settlement ledger**, and **RegTech AI** for AML scoring—future‑proof for stable‑coin or token‑based settlement when regulators permit. **Bottom line:** By aligning **global standards** with **regional adaptations**, the firm can keep **compliance costs ≤ 10 % of revenue**, **maintain ≥ 2 % net margin**, and **grow cross‑border volume by 30 % YoY** while safely navigating divergent licensing regimes, capital‑control constraints, and partner‑technology gaps.

Each bloc now enforces distinct licensing, KYC, and settlement-currency rules, and several corridors face new capital-control measures. Design a financial-operations strategy for sustaining and expanding cross-border payment corridors under divergent licensing regimes, balancing compliance cost, settlement risk, and partner economics across regions.

• **Export‑as‑XML** for regulator portals. | One‑click generation of **EU‑TSR**, **GCC‑AML**, **MAS‑Monthly**, **BCB‑FX** reports. | > **Result:** A **single compliance platform** (core) with **plug‑in adapters** for each jurisdiction, dramatically reducing duplicated effort and licence‑maintenance cost. --- ## 3. Settlement‑Risk & Liquidity Management ### 3.1 Core Principles | Principle | Implementation | |-----------|----------------| | **Local‑Currency Settlement** wherever legally required | Maintain **regional liquidity pools** in EUR, AED, SAR, SGD, IDR, BRL, MXN, etc. | | **FX‑Hedging at Margin‑Optimal Frequency** | Use **FX‑forward contracts** and **non‑deliverable forwards (NDFs)** aligned with daily settlement windows; hedge **only the net exposure** after intra‑bloc netting. | | **Dual‑Bank Settlement Model** | **Primary settlement bank** (high‑tech, low‑cost) + **fallback “bridge bank”** (local partner) to mitigate operational outages. | | **Capital‑Control Buffer** | Pre‑allocate **regulatory‑approved capital** (e.g., 5 % of daily outbound volume) in a **restricted‑purpose account** that can be instantly moved under local approval. | | **Real‑Time Settlement Engine** | Deploy a **micro‑service** (e.g., **ISO‑20022** API) that executes **instant FX** and **settlement** in < 5 seconds for high‑volume corridors (EU ↔ Gulf). | ### 3.2 Corridor‑Specific Settlement Blueprint | Corridor | Settlement Currency(s) | Liquidity‑Pool Size (10 M USD‑equiv) | Hedging Tool | Capital‑Control Treatment | |----------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------|---------------------------| | **EU → Gulf** | EUR → AED/SAR (via USD bridge) | €5 M (EU) / AED 4 M (Gulf) | NDF on USD‑AED, USD‑SAR; **Daily forward** to lock rate | Outbound USD > $50 k flagged → **pre‑authorisation** via Gulf sponsor bank | | **Gulf → EU** | AED/SAR → EUR (USD bridge) | AED 4 M / €5 M | **FX‑forward** on USD‑EUR, **FX‑option** for vol‑spike | Inbound USD caps lifted if **local bank** certifies compliance | | **EU → SEA** | EUR → SGD/IDR/VND/PH‑(USD) | €3 M (EU) / SGD 6 M (SG) | **NDF** for IDR, VND; **FX‑option** for high‑vol markets | Vietnam monthly USD ≤ $100 k → **monthly limit manager** | | **LATAM → EU** | BRL/MXN/PEN → EUR (USD bridge) | BRL 4 M / MXN 5 M / €6 M | **NDF** for BRL‑USD, MXN‑USD; **FX‑forward** for EUR | Brazil IOF tax auto‑applied; MXN caps managed via **Bank‑approved quota** | | **EU → LATAM** | EUR → BRL/MXN/PEN (USD bridge) | €6 M / BRL 5 M | Same tools as above | Same capital‑control handling (tax, quotas) | > **Liquidity‑Pool Funding:** Use **core‑bank credit lines** (Euro‑area syndicated facility) and **regional bank credit lines** (Gulf‑region, SEA, LATAM) to fund pools. Set **interest‑rate spread** based on corridor margin (see Section 4). --- ## 4. Partner‑Economics & Technical Enablement ### 4.1 Partner‑Selection Matrix | Partner Tier | Technical Maturity | Economic Terms | Typical Role | Example Partners (2026) | |--------------|-------------------|----------------|--------------|-------------------------| | **Tier 1 – “Smart‑Bank”** | Full ISO‑20022, real‑time API, sandbox access, 99.9 % uptime | **Revenue‑share 20 %** of net margin, **cost‑plus** settlement fee (0.05 % of value) | Primary settlement, FX execution, compliance‑screening | BNP Paribas (EU), Emirates NBD (Gulf), DBS (SEA), Banco do Brasil (LATAM) | | **Tier 2 – “Legacy‑Bank”** | Batch file (MT‑103/MT‑202), 1‑day latency, limited API | **Revenue‑share 15 %**, higher settlement fee (0.10 %) | Backup settlement, large‑ticket processing | UniCredit (EU), National Commercial Bank (UAE), BNI (Indonesia), Bancomer (Mexico) | | **Tier 3 – “FinTech‑Overlay”** | API‑first, programmable money, token‑isation, crypto‑friendly | **Revenue‑share 12‑18 %**, **per‑transaction fee** (flat $0.30) | Front‑end payment collection, on‑ramp/off‑ramp, digital‑wallet integration | TransferWise (now Wise), Rapyd, Binance‑Pay, PayU (LATAM) | | **Tier 4 – “Bridge/Correspondent”** | Limited connectivity, manual SWIFT, no API | **Revenue‑share 10 %**, **high fee** (0.25 %) | “Last‑mile” for low‑volume corridors, compliance‑audit support | Small regional banks, credit‑unions | > **Economic Target:** Keep **overall corridor net margin** > 2 % after partner fees, FX cost, and compliance overhead. ### 4.2 Partner‑Enablement Programme 1. **API‑Standardisation Kit** – ISO‑20022‑based **JSON** payloads, **OAuth 2.0** security, **OpenAPI** spec shared with all partners. 2. **Technical Maturity Scorecard** – quarterly assessment; tier‑up partners who meet **≥ 90 %** of the spec (automatic fee reduction). 3. **Co‑Funding of Sandbox** – allocate **$250 k** per region to help Tier‑2/3 banks build real‑time APIs; ROI measured by **settlement‑time reduction** (target < 5 sec). 4. **Revenue‑Sharing Review** – annual renegotiation based on **volume‑weighting**; high‑volume corridors (EU ↔ Gulf) move toward **cost‑plus** model, low‑volume corridors stay **revenue‑share**. --- ## 5. Margin & Pricing Model (Cost‑Based + Risk‑Adjusted) | Cost Component | How it is Calculated | Weight in Pricing (example) | |----------------|---------------------|----------------------------| | **Licensing & Reg‑Compliance** | Fixed annual licence fee + per‑transaction compliance cost (average $0.02) | 15 % | | **Partner Settlement Fee** | Tier‑specific fee (see Table 4.1) + FX‑spread | 30 % | | **FX‑Hedging Cost** | Forward points + option premium / transaction value | 20 % | | **Capital‑Control Buffer Cost** | Opportunity cost of locked‑up capital (average 2 % p.a.) | 10 % | | **Operational Overhead** | Cloud, monitoring, staff, fraud‑prevention | 15 % | | **Profit Margin** | Target **≥ 2 %** net after all above | 10 % | > **Dynamic Pricing Engine** – a **micro‑service** that pulls real‑time cost inputs (FX forward curve, partner fee APIs, compliance‑cost per‑transaction) and outputs the **customer‑visible price** (exchange rate + fee). The engine enforces **minimum‑margin thresholds** per corridor (e.g., EU ↔ Gulf min 2.5 %, LATAM ↔ EU min 1.8 %) to protect profitability. --- ## 6. Risk Management Framework | Risk Category | Primary Exposure | Mitigation Controls | |---------------|------------------|---------------------| | **Regulatory Risk** | License revocation, sanction breaches | • **Regulatory Calendar** (auto‑reminders for filing, capital‑adequacy reports).
• **RegTech** alerts for rule‑change (e.g., EU‑PSD3 draft). | | **Settlement‑Risk** | Counter‑party default, FX settlement fail | • **Dual‑Bank** model, **real‑time netting** engine.
• **Credit limit monitoring** per partner (auto‑pause on breach). | | **Capital‑Control Risk** | Outbound caps, sudden policy shifts | • **Capital‑Control Buffer** (pre‑authorised cash).
• **Dynamic routing** (switch to alternative corridor). | | **Operational / Tech Risk** | API downtime, data‑loss, cyber‑attack | • **Zero‑trust network**, **SOC‑2** compliance, **API‑gateway throttling**.
• **Disaster‑Recovery (DR) site** per region (fail‑over < 30 sec). | | **Fraud / Money‑Laundering** | Synthetic IDs, circular transactions | • **AI‑risk‑scorer**, **behavioural analytics**, **real‑time transaction monitoring**.
• **Manual escalation** to local sponsor bank AML team. | | **Liquidity Risk** | Insufficient local‑currency pool | • **Liquidity Management Dashboard** (real‑time pool balances).

RANM must stay **> 1 %** for a corridor to stay open. --- ## 7. Expansion Roadmap (2026‑2028) | Year | Milestone | Action | Expected Impact | |------|-----------|--------|-----------------| | **2026 Q1** | **Core Platform Launch** (RegTech hub, settlement engine) | Deploy in EU & Gulf (first two corridors) | Baseline compliance cost ↓ 30 % | | **2026 Q2** | **Partner‑Upgrade Sprint** (Tier‑2 banking API enablement) | Co‑fund sandbox with 3 Gulf banks & 2 SEA banks | Settlement latency ↓ 70 % | | **2026 Q3** | **Capital‑Control Buffer** activation for Indonesia & Brazil | Pre‑authorize $10 M pooled funds per region | Outbound cap breaches ↓ 90 % | | **2026 Q4** | **New Corridor Pilot** – **EU ↔ Mexico** | Obtain Mexican “FinTech” licence, integrate Banca Azteca as Tier‑3 partner | Test regulatory‑flex model, add $12 M ARR | | **2027 H1** | **Dynamic Pricing Engine** goes live across all corridors | Real‑time cost‑feed integration | Margin volatility ↓ 15 % | | **2027 H2** | **Regulatory‑Change Automation** – AI‑driven rule extraction from new EU‑PSD3 drafts | Reduce manual rule‑coding time from weeks to days | Compliance lag < 48 h | | **2028 Q1** | **Full‑Corridor Coverage** – Add **EU ↔ Vietnam**, **Gulf ↔ Peru** | Leverage existing platform; rely on Tier‑2 banks after API upgrade | Total cross‑border volume + 45 % | | **2028 H2** | **Strategic Review** – Consolidate **Tier‑1** partners, drop under‑performing Tier‑4 banks | Re‑negotiate revenue‑share, re‑allocate liquidity | Cost‑to‑serve ↓ 12 % | --- ## 8. Governance & Operating Model | Committee | Frequency | Scope | Decision Rights | |----------|-----------|-------|-----------------| | **Global AI‑Col‑Council** (CEO, CFO, Chief Regulatory Officer, Head of Payments Ops) | Monthly | Overall strategy, capital allocation, major licensing decisions | Approve new licences, major partner contracts | | **Regional Regulation Boards** (EU, Gulf, SEA, LATAM) | Bi‑monthly | Local licence renewals, KYC policy tweaks, capital‑control liaison | Sign off any region‑specific compliance changes | | **Partner‑Performance Review Board** | Quarterly | Tier‑up/down decisions, fee renegotiation, technical maturity | Adjust partner tier, set fee schedule | | **Risk‑Ops Committee** | Weekly | Real‑time risk flags, liquidity shortfalls, fraud incidents | Issue stop‑payment orders, adjust limits | | **Product & Pricing Council** | Monthly | Pricing engine parameters, margin thresholds, new‑corridor proposals | Approve price changes across corridors | > **Reporting:** A **central “Operations Dashboard”** (Power‑BI) feeds live KPI to all committees: **Volume, Net Margin, RANM, Compliance‑Cost, Partner‑Uptime, Capital‑Control Utilisation**. --- ## Prioritise **Tier 1 “Smart‑Banks”** for high‑margin, high‑volume corridors; use **Tier 2/3 partners** to expand low‑volume lanes while still meeting SLA targets. 5. **Institutionalise a dynamic pricing engine** that pulls real‑time costs (FX, partner fees, compliance) and enforces a **minimum‑margin guardrail** per corridor. 6. **Implement a risk‑adjusted net‑margin (RANM) metric** to continuously evaluate whether a corridor should stay open, be re‑priced, or be re‑engineered. 7. **Launch the platform in two “anchor” corridors** (EU ↔ Gulf, EU ↔ SEA) in 2026 Q1–Q4, then roll out additional corridors (Latin‑America, Vietnam, Mexico) with the same compliance core but local partner upgrades. 8. **Governance:** Set up a **global‑regional dual committee structure** for licensing, compliance, partner performance, and risk monitoring; feed a **central dashboard** to all decision‑makers. 9. **Technology:** Leverage **cloud‑native ISO‑20022 micro‑services**, a **Corda‑based settlement ledger**, and **RegTech AI** for AML scoring—future‑proof for stable‑coin or token‑based settlement when regulators permit. **Bottom line:** By aligning **global standards** with **regional adaptations**, the firm can keep **compliance costs ≤ 10 % of revenue**, **maintain ≥ 2 % net margin**, and **grow cross‑border volume by 30 % YoY** while safely navigating divergent licensing regimes, capital‑control constraints, and partner‑technology gaps.
